phase: Movement-system replacement. Clone Elite Dangerous supercruise as the starting point for ALL in-system motion (Max's scope pick: post-warp fly-in + tour legs + COMMIT BURN transit), rewire the autopilot to drive it, add Elite-style hold-to-look freelook. One flight model, two drivers (autopilot / player). Ship transform and head/camera mount separated from day one so the near-future cockpit attaches without motion rework. Arrival keeps today's shaking-fast-decel beat (accel the inverse) ported onto the new model. AutopilotMotion and FlythroughCamera's motion role retire. Integration seam: warpRevealSystem nav handoff (main.js ~5510, per docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-warp-arrival-billboard-distance-design.md). Out of scope: cockpit visual, world-origin rebasing, time dilation, wide binaries, warp-tunnel changes.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The supercruise flight model, cloned from Elite as the starting point: the ship always advances along its nose vector; throttle sets target speed; max speed scales with distance from massive bodies (crawl near a planet, enormous in deep space); acceleration/deceleration is heavy and smooth (no instant speed changes); turn rate is capped and tightens as speed rises.

verifyVia.input: Headless Vitest suite driving the flight model in isolation: step the model with fixed throttle/steering inputs near a massive body vs in deep space; step turn inputs at low vs high speed.
verifyVia.observable: Position delta is always along the nose vector; speed asymptotically approaches the throttle-set target (bounded accel, no step change); the gravity-well speed cap is monotonically increasing with distance from the dominant body; achieved turn rate never exceeds the cap and the cap at high speed is lower than at low speed.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Player movement is independent of the freelook system, and the systems allow for the future cockpit inclusion: the ship entity transform is the single authoritative source of motion; the camera/head is a mount deriving from it; freelook writes only to the mount, never to the ship.

verifyVia.input: Headless test: fly the model on a fixed trajectory while applying freelook input to the head mount; then a cockpit-attachment probe — parent a dummy object to the ship transform.
verifyVia.observable: Ship trajectory (position + heading series) is bit-identical with and without freelook input; the dummy 'cockpit' object tracks ship position+orientation exactly while the head mount rotates independently of both.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Manual piloting works in the running game: mouse acts as a virtual joystick (deflection from center = pitch/yaw turn rate, capped) with an on-screen indicator; W/S set throttle (Elite convention); the player can fly to a body, decelerate into the drop window, and arrive — coming in too hot overshoots.

verifyVia.input: Live (GPU 9223 chrome-devtools, per memory/well-dipper-testing-reference.md): take manual control, inject synthetic mouse/keyboard input to fly toward a planet — one approach inside the drop window, one deliberately too fast.
verifyVia.observable: Ship turns at a rate proportional to mouse deflection (capped); throttle responds to W/S; the in-window approach ends in arrival at the body (orbit/idle behavior engaged at the expected capture distance); the too-hot approach overshoots (passes the body without capture); HUD joystick indicator tracks the injected deflection.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Freelook, basically like Elite: holding the freelook control swings the view freely while the ship keeps flying its line; releasing recenters the view forward.

verifyVia.input: Live: during supercruise flight (autopilot or manual), hold the freelook control and inject mouse movement; release; sample ship heading, ship trajectory, and camera orientation per frame throughout.
verifyVia.observable: While held: camera orientation diverges from ship heading by the injected amount while ship velocity direction and trajectory are unchanged versus a no-freelook control run; on release: camera orientation returns to ship-forward (eased recenter), ending aligned within tolerance.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The autopilot is rewired to drive the supercruise system in place of what's there today: the post-warp fly-in, the system-tour legs between bodies, and the nav-computer COMMIT BURN transit are all flown by the autopilot working the same throttle/steering/drop controls a player would. AutopilotMotion and FlythroughCamera's motion role are retired from the live path.

verifyVia.input: Live: (a) warp to a fresh system and let the tour run through ≥2 stops; (b) trigger COMMIT BURN to a planet via the nav computer. Instrument which mover writes camera/ship position each frame.
verifyVia.observable: Every in-system motion frame is written by the supercruise ship entity (autopilot inputs visible on the model: throttle/turn commands within the same caps as manual); zero frames written by AutopilotMotion or FlythroughCamera travel during fly-in, tour legs, and COMMIT BURN; each leg ends with the drop/arrival behavior at the target body.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Today's felt beats survive on the new model: arrival is a shaking, fast decel; acceleration is the inverse. Departure ramps with shake, arrival decelerates hard with shake, cruise between is smooth.

verifyVia.input: Live: ride one autopilot tour leg end-to-end; sample speed and the camera-shake driver state per frame.
verifyVia.observable: Speed profile shows a steep (but continuous) decel into arrival and the mirrored ramp on departure; the shake driver is active during the accel and decel windows and quiescent mid-cruise.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Minimal screen-space HUD: speed readout, throttle indicator, virtual-joystick reticle, and a target marker with the drop window — present and tracking live state during supercruise (screen-space, so it survives the future cockpit swap).

verifyVia.input: Live: during manual flight with a locked target, inject throttle and steering changes; read the HUD DOM/canvas elements and the flight-model state each frame.
verifyVia.observable: HUD speed equals model speed; throttle indicator equals commanded throttle; joystick reticle position equals current mouse deflection; target marker tracks the target's screen position and the drop-window state (in-window vs too-fast) matches the model's.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Nothing the screensaver does today regresses: title → warp → arrival at billboard distance → autopilot tour → auto-warp loops unattended across systems; Toy Box mode and the mobile always-Toy-Box constraint are untouched.

verifyVia.input: Live: from a fresh load, let the loop run unattended across ≥2 complete system visits (tour + auto-warp); separately verify Toy Box orbit/zoom on a focused body and the isMobile constructor constraint (headless for the constraint).
verifyVia.observable: Both auto-warps complete with the destination star(s) in billboard LOD at emergence (system.star billboard visible, per the shipped arrival-distance invariant); both tours complete and re-warp without input; no AC4/AC5 portal warnings and no new console errors; Toy Box drag/zoom behavior unchanged; mobile path still forces TOY_BOX.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Flying it manually and watching the autopilot fly it, the whole thing reads as Elite supercruise: pointing the nose with the mouse feels like Elite's virtual stick, the gravity-well slowdown near bodies feels right, freelook feels like Elite's headlook, the shaking accel/decel beats land, and the screensaver tour looks at least as good as before.

verifyVia.input: Max flies: takes manual control, cruises to a planet, drops out; overshoots once on purpose; uses freelook mid-flight; then hands off and watches the autopilot run a full tour + auto-warp.
verifyVia.observable: Holistic acceptance — does this cohere as the Elite-style flight experience Max wanted. Deferred to Max.
